newsitem.title: FRANCE: Historian Francois Furet elected to French Academy.
newsitem.headline: Historian Francois Furet elected to French Academy.

text.p: Historian Francois Furet, an expert on the French Revolution and on communism, was elected to the prestigious French Academy on Thursday, replacing the late prime minister Michel Debre who died last year.

Furet, 69, a professor at France's Higher School of Social Studies and at the University of Chicago, published an acclaimed history of communist thought and its intellectual fellow travellers in 1995 entitled "The Past of an Illusion".
The book considers communist ideology as a kind of secular substitute for religion.
A former communist, he quit the French party after Soviet troops crushed the 1956 Hungarian uprising.

Furet is the author of numerous works on the French Revolution including the ground-breaking historiography "Penser la Revolution francaise" (The French Revolution in Thought), and a "Critical Dictionary of the French Revolution", written jointly with Mona Ozouff.
The 40-member academy, created by Cardinal Richelieu in the 17th century, is France's most revered body of writers, thinkers and cultural figures.
